e: Run the steady, always-on baseline on regular Fargate for availability, and use Fargate Spot (a discount, but interruptible) for the short traffic bursts, balancing availability and cost through a capacity provider strategy. Spot for the baseline risks availability, and rightsizing alone doesn't add the discount.

AWS Shield Advanced is the managed DDoS protection service with proactive engagement from the Shield Response Team and cost protection; ALB and Route 53 hosted zones can be protected resources. WAF, Config, and GuardDuty don't provide that proactive DDoS engagement.

NLBs now support security groups, so recreating the NLB with a security group that allows only trusted IP addresses blocks unauthorized access with minimal architectural change. WAF can't attach to an NLB, and Shield or a second NLB don't restrict access that way.

The Lambda execution role needs IAM permissions to publish to SNS and to use the customer managed KMS key, the SNS topic policy must allow the function to publish, and the KMS key policy must allow SNS and the publisher to use the key for encryption and decryption. API Gateway and swapping to AWS managed keys don't address this.

Keep the portal on EC2 On-Demand instances in an Auto Scaling group (100% uptime, no code changes) and run the infrequent, on-demand document extraction in Lambda, triggered when a document is uploaded, so you pay only when it runs. Spot instances can be interrupted, and moving the portal to S3 and API Gateway needs code changes.

For cross-account SNS-to-Lambda delivery, the Lambda function's resource-based policy must allow SNS to invoke it, and the SNS topic policy must allow the function (the administrator account) to subscribe. EventBridge or Athena don't deliver SNS messages to the function.

The Amazon VPC CNI plugin for Kubernetes supports custom networking, letting pods use secondary ENIs in custom subnets within the VPC and communicate securely with other VPC resources. Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, or Kubernetes network policies and anti-affinity don't set pod subnets.

Modifying the existing RDS instance to a Multi-AZ deployment adds a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone with automatic failover, and it's a single setting applied in the maintenance window. Migrating engines, restoring snapshots, or running the database in an Auto Scaling group is much more effort.

Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a managed file service that supports SMB and NFS simultaneously on the same data (multi-protocol access) with Multi-AZ redundancy. FSx for Lustre doesn't support SMB, and EC2 or S3 File Gateway options don't give shared multi-protocol managed storage.

An Auto Scaling group of private EC2 instances in multiple AZs behind an ALB makes the web tier scalable and highly available, and Aurora MySQL with a primary and a reader in separate AZs makes the database highly available and offloads reads to cut read latency. Multi-Region options add cost and complexity.

AWS Secrets Manager stores sensitive values securely and rotates them automatically, and a Lambda layer that retrieves the secret gives all of the thousands of functions one shared way to fetch it with little per-function work. Parameter Store lacks native rotation, and the other options don't manage rotation.

AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, and EBS volumes and recommends rightsizing with estimated savings, in one service with no reports to search. Cost and Usage Reports and billing alerts don't give recommendations.

Amazon EFS is a high-performing shared file system that instances in multiple Availability Zones can mount concurrently, with its mount targets inside the VPC. S3 isn't mounted as a volume natively, and EBS volumes can't be shared across AZs this way.

The primary stays at a steady 60% CPU, so leave it alone, and the read replica at only 25% CPU can be downsized to a smaller instance to save cost while still serving reporting reads with room for growth. Deleting the replica would put the reports back on the primary.

For long-running steady workloads, the deepest discounts come from 3-year terms with All Upfront payment: RDS Reserved Instances for the database and an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the instances. Shorter terms or no-upfront options cost more, and On-Demand RDS costs the most.

IRSA works by creating an IAM role with the needed permissions and a trust relationship with the cluster's OIDC identity provider, then annotating the Kubernetes service account with the role's ARN so pods get granular, temporary credentials. Node role policies or cluster role changes are too broad.

SSE-KMS with the AWS managed key for S3 rotates the key automatically every year, key usage and rotation are logged in CloudTrail, and AWS managed keys have no monthly key fee, which minimizes cost. SSE-S3 doesn't give CloudTrail key visibility, SSE-C isn't rotated by AWS, and customer managed keys add a monthly charge.

Tag resources with an application key, activate the tags as cost allocation tags, and use Cost Explorer (with its saved reports) to break down costs per application on a regular basis, at no additional infrastructure cost. RDS-based analysis or manual bill downloads are laborious.

An Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs, a Multi-AZ RDS instance, and CloudFront with S3 for static assets eliminates single points of failure at every tier. Single-AZ designs, serving assets from EC2, or One Zone storage aren't resilient.

A Gateway Load Balancer in the networking account fronting the security appliance, reached through Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in the application accounts, transparently inspects traffic between applications across accounts. NLBs, ALBs, or plain interface endpoints don't provide transparent appliance insertion.

An Aurora custom endpoint can include a chosen subset of replicas (those three), load-balancing connections across just those instances, which suits a workload that needs specific instance sizes. The reader endpoint spreads across all replicas, and instance endpoints don't balance.

AWS Secrets Manager stores the database credentials and has built-in automatic rotation for RDS PostgreSQL, and the Lambda function just retrieves the secret, with the least operational overhead. Parameter Store has no automatic rotation, and custom rotation functions or KMS keys aren't a credential store.

AWS DMS Serverless automatically provisions and scales replication capacity up and down with the workload, so you pay only for the capacity required. Multi-AZ replication instances, EC2 Auto Scaling, or Fargate don't scale a DMS replication instance this way.

AWS PrivateLink creates private connectivity from the VPC to a SaaS provider's endpoint service over the AWS network, with minimal public internet exposure and no VPN or routing setup. VPN and Transit Gateway don't connect to a provider's service this way.

A Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec, which encrypts traffic at the network and session layers, and route tables with security groups and network ACLs restrict access to only the required traffic. Direct Connect isn't encrypted by default, and IAM policies or Transit Gateway alone don't provide encryption.
